extraction.name: RoboBench
extraction.description: A benchmark for systematically evaluating multimodal large language models as embodied brains for robotic manipulation. It contains 6092 QA pairs across five dimensions—instruction comprehension, perception reasoning, generalized planning, affordance prediction, and failure analysis—covering 14 capabilities and 25 tasks. Data span diverse embodiments, attribute-rich objects, multi-view scenes, and memory-driven navigation.
extraction.creator: Yulin Luo; Chun-Kai Fan; Menghang Dong; Jiayu Shi; Mengdi Zhao; Bo-Wen Zhang; Cheng Chi; Jiaming Liu; Gaole Dai; Rongyu Zhang; Ruichuan An; Kun Wu; Zhengping Che; Shaoxuan Xie; Guocai Yao; Zhongxia Zhao; Pengwei Wang; Guang Liu; Zhongyuan Wang; Tiejun Huang; Shanghang Zhang
extraction.citeAs: Yulin Luo et al. RoboBench: A Comprehensive Evaluation Benchmark for Multimodal Large Language Models as Embodied Brain. arXiv:2510.17801v1 [cs.RO], 20 October 2025.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The benchmark combines open-source, large-scale real-world robotic datasets with curated in-house robotic data. High-quality robotic videos form a planning pool, from which frame sequences and representative frames are extracted. Real robot data and associated type and viewpoint metadata support perception tasks. Execution-level failure examples are collected from RoboMIND. Data are enriched with MLLM-generated and human-provided annotations and converted into task-specific QA formats.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Physical data collection, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw sources include open-source robotic datasets and in-house robotic collection, consisting of robotic videos, images, and metadata. Cited sources include Open X-Embodiment, RH20T, RoboMIND, and AgiBot World Colosseo. Static object attributes are drawn from curated data referenced to Gao et al. (2024). Execution-level failure examples come from RoboMIND.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: LLMs rewrite explicit instructions into paired implicit, demand-based requests while retaining the images and ground truth. Planning-level failures are synthesized by perturbing correct instructions through wrong-object substitutions, missing steps, and incorrect ordering. Natural-language action descriptions are mapped to predefined manipulation or navigation function templates, whose arguments are instantiated with extracted object references.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Robotic videos are converted into frame sequences as standardized inputs, and representative frames are sampled for affordance tasks. Construction-stage filtering applies general criteria for image quality and task validity, alongside task-specific rules such as excluding single-arm data from dual-arm tasks. Perception data are standardized into multiple-choice QA. Following construction, items solved correctly by all models are removed, while items all models fail to solve undergo manual review and correction.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Gemini generates task summaries, timestamped step-wise instructions, and metadata describing objects, actions, scenes, and embodiments; human annotators refine these outputs. Robot type and viewpoint metadata support template-based QA. Object-centric annotations combine curated static attributes with GPT-generated functional properties and distractors. Gemini segments videos for temporal grounding; humans annotate relative positions, keypoint changes, and bounding boxes connecting instructions to target objects. Sampled frames are annotated with static contact points, dynamic motion trajectories, and mobile robot base positions. Experts label execution-level failures. Directed acyclic graphs capturing planning dependencies are manually annotated. Twenty professionally trained annotators inspect linguistic clarity, answerability, and correctness.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Machine-generated planning annotations are refined by humans. Quality control includes construction-stage filtering and post-construction validation by 20 professionally trained annotators. The authors describe a majority-vote strategy in which items all models solve correctly are removed, whereas items all models fail to solve receive manual review and correction.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: The paper describes 20 professionally trained annotators conducting quality inspections, experts labeling execution-level failures, and expert annotators with prior training participating in the planning-metric human study. No age, gender, nationality, or other demographic characteristics are reported.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Gemini for video segmentation, task summaries, timestamped step descriptions, and structured metadata; GPT for functional properties and distractors; unspecified LLMs for explicit-to-implicit instruction rewriting; unspecified detection models mentioned in the construction pipeline.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Planning-level failure examples are synthesized because real-world planning failure data are lacking. The paper also notes limits of the current evaluation and substantial variation in difficulty across dimensions; execution-level failure diagnosis is difficult even for human evaluators.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Testing and benchmarking multimodal large language models as high-level embodied brains for robotic manipulation across instruction comprehension, perception reasoning, generalized planning, affordance prediction, and failure analysis. Planning tasks assess full action-sequence prediction, next-step prediction, and subtask completion estimation. Perception and failure tasks use multiple-choice accuracy; affordance tasks evaluate point and trajectory prediction. Long-horizon planning is evaluated using an MLLM-as-world-simulator framework with reference action lists and human-annotated dependency graphs to assess structural correctness and embodied feasibility. The benchmark is intended to identify cognitive bottlenecks and guide development of more robust, generalizable robotic intelligence.
